title: The Airpower We Need for Irregular Warfare
gist: A CNAS-promoted Irregular Warfare Initiative podcast examines why giving aircraft to partner forces often fails to produce an effective air force, drawing on Tobias Switzer's RAND report 'Build Partner Airpower, Not Air Forces' and lessons from US air advisors in Iraq and Afghanistan. The page also notes CNAS research that US veterans fell from 21.0 million in 2015 to 17.3 million in 2026.

insights.claim: Providing aircraft to partner forces frequently falls short of building an effective air force because there is a gap between acquiring technology and turning it into military power.
insights.speaker: CNAS
insights.so_what: Security-assistance aircraft sales do not guarantee partner capability — temper expectations for outcomes of foreign military sales programs.

insights.claim: Tobias Switzer's RAND report argues the US should 'Build Partner Airpower, Not Air Forces', a framework informed by what American air advisors learned in Iraq and Afghanistan.
insights.speaker: CNAS
insights.so_what: Points to a shift in US security-cooperation design toward capability-focused rather than platform-focused aid.

insights.claim: The US veteran population fell to 17.3 million in 2026 from 21.0 million in 2015 as older, conscription-era veterans age out.
insights.speaker: CNAS
insights.so_what: Shrinking veteran base affects recruitment pipelines and civil-military ties over time.
